transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
You multiplied speed by time, but the units don't match—what unit is the speed in, and what unit should it be to match the time?
Its in km per hour. I dont know, does that matter? Distance is speed times time, right?
Okay, let me think.
Yes, distance is speed times time, but the units must match. If speed is in km per hour, time must be in hours too.
I dont get why though. The formula is right, why does it care about units?
Good question. One moment.

Units matter because you can only multiply quantities that have compatible units. For example, if you walk at 5 meters per second for 3 seconds, you go 15 meters. Can you apply that to your car problem?
Not really. Mine is km per hour and seconds. I dont know what to do with that.
Let me see.
Units must match to multiply them. For example, if you go 60 km per hour for 1 hour, you travel 60 km. What unit should you convert 5.0 seconds to so it matches km per hour?
Hours? So 5 seconds is 5 over 3600 hours? Then 72 times that is like 0.1 km?
Got it. Give me a second.
Units must match to multiply. For example, if you go 60 km per hour for 1 hour, you travel 60 km. What unit should you convert 5.0 seconds to so it matches km per hour?
I said hours. So d is 72 times 5 over 3600, 0.1 km, which is 100 meters. Is that right?
Okay, let me think.
You're right that time must be in hours, but your final answer is off. The units must match before you multiply.
Off how? 72 times 5 is 360, divided by 3600 is 0.1 km. Thats 100 m.
Good question. One moment.
Units must match before you multiply. For example, if you go 10 km per hour for 1 hour, you go 10 km. What unit should you convert 5.0 seconds to so it matches km per hour?
Hours, I did that. Im writing 100 m as my answer. Bye.
Let me see.
Units must match before you multiply. For example, if you go 10 km per hour for 1 hour, you travel 10 km. What unit should you convert 5.0 seconds to so it matches km per hour?
